title: Convert 3MF to STL
description: Convert a 3MF model to STL for slicers and geometry-only 3D printing workflows.
heading: When to use STL instead of 3MF
body: 3MF can store units, multiple objects, materials and other printing information. STL stores triangle geometry only. Use STL when your slicer or downstream tool requires it; otherwise keeping the original 3MF may preserve more information.
check: Compare the exported dimensions with your original model in your slicer. STL has no unit metadata; this converter writes millimetre coordinates.

title: Convert OBJ to STL
description: Export OBJ triangle geometry to STL for 3D printing and mesh workflows.
heading: Geometry rather than textures
body: OBJ can refer to MTL files and external textures. STL cannot carry these materials. If your OBJ came in a folder, use the model-package tool to keep its dependencies available during import.
check: OBJ does not define physical units. Check the size, closed surfaces and orientation in your slicer before printing.

title: Convert FBX to STL
description: Export a static mesh from an FBX scene as STL for printing and geometry workflows.
heading: From an animated scene to a static mesh
body: FBX may contain rigs, animation, materials and multiple objects. STL represents static surface triangles. Select or prepare the intended pose and geometry before exporting; animation and appearance will not survive the STL format.
check: Inspect the exported mesh for separate shells, scale and thin features. A successful format conversion is not a printability check.

title: Convert GLB to STL
description: Convert a GLB scene into static STL geometry for use in a slicer.
heading: From a web model to printable geometry
body: GLB can contain meshes, textures, materials and animation in one file. STL retains static triangle geometry, without textures or animation. The conversion does not automatically make a model watertight.
check: Check model size, wall thickness and non-manifold edges in your slicer. The STL export uses millimetre coordinates.

title: Compress an STL file
description: Reduce STL file size using same-format mesh compression without a format change.
heading: Balance file size and geometry detail
body: STL size depends largely on triangle count. The mesh compression presets may simplify static geometry, so a smaller file can lose fine features. Keep an original copy and choose the lightest useful compression level.
check: Compare the result in your slicer before printing. If the candidate is not smaller, the original is retained.

title: Compress a 3MF file
description: Recompress a 3MF package without changing its format or deliberately simplifying its geometry.
heading: Keep the model package intact
body: 3MF is already a ZIP-based package. Lossless recompression changes how its entries are stored, not the geometry or texture contents. Some already-compressed packages may not become smaller.
check: Keep the original file. The converter retains it when lossless recompression cannot reduce the size.
